newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan foreign aid to be more selective - MOF chief.
newsitem.headline: Japan foreign aid to be more selective - MOF chief.

text.p: Japan intends to be more selective in allocating official development assistance (ODA) as the nation is carrying out fiscal reforms, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Friday.
He told a news conference he conveyed this message to Inter-American Development Bank (IADB) President Enrique Iglesias in a brief meeting earlier on Friday.
Mitsuzuka explained about Japan's fiscal reform plans including a 10 percent cut in the country's ODA in the next fiscal year, starting on April 1, 1998.
"Given the limited budget, we will deal with foreign aid after hearing requests from needy countries, and we will deal with them if those requests are extremely important projects," Mitsuzuka said.
Iglesias, in Japan to attend an international conference on international organisations, is also meeting Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto during his stay.
